newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan stocks end up on foreign fund hope.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan stocks end up on foreign fund hope.

text.p: Taiwan share prices closed higher on Tuesday on hopes that more foreign funds may enter ahead of Morgan Stanley's planned schedule to include Taiwan in its global stock indices from September 2, brokers said.
The index ended up 32.05 points or 0.52 percent at 6,232.53. Turnover was a modest T$27.02 billion.
The local Commercial Times newspaper said on Tuesday that foreign funds had remitted inward more than US$200 million in the past 10 days.
"Such hope for foreign fund entries should continue to push up the index steadily," said Michael Hung of Nikko Securities.
"Several foreign fund managers in Singapore told me that they plan to remit money into Taiwan in the week starting September 2," Hung said, who visited Singapore last week.
Electronics led the gains on expected sound August sales and profit performance, with Accton up T$3 to T$56.5.
Cements, textiles and financials were also strong.
Textile firm Li Peng, which makes drawn texturized yarn, rose by the daily seven percent limit to T$21.7.
"Personal computer, construction and drawn texturized yarn companies are expected to have improved fundamentals in coming months, and they should be the focus of bargain hunting," Hung said.
Because of foreign fund hopes, brokers said they expected a firming trend to test resistance at 6,400.
For Wednesday, a 6,200-6,270 range was seen.
